---
title: "Styling a Quarto Website with CSS and SCSS"
---

## Why would I style my website beyond a built-in theme?

Quarto ships with Bootswatch themes (like `cosmo`, which this site starts from), but a theme looks like everyone else's site. CSS and SCSS let me add a consistent brand: colors, fonts, spacing, and reusable components. This whole site uses the green and gold from our CEP presentation.

## What is the difference between CSS and SCSS?

::: {.panel-tabset}

### CSS

Plain CSS is a list of rules. It is loaded with `css:` in the YAML and applied on top of the theme.

```{.yaml}
format:
  html:
    theme: cosmo
    css: styles.css
```

```{.css}
.highlight {
  background: #FAF6EE;
  border-left: 5px solid #C48A3A;
}
```

### SCSS

SCSS (Sass) adds variables, nesting, and the ability to change the theme's own settings. It is loaded inside `theme:` and has two sections.

```{.yaml}
format:
  html:
    theme: [cosmo, styles.scss]
```

```{.scss}
/*-- scss:defaults --*/
$farm-green: #1F3A2E;
$primary: $farm-green;      // changes the navbar, buttons, and links

/*-- scss:rules --*/
.highlight {
  border-left: 5px solid #C48A3A;
}
```

:::

## When do I use `scss:defaults` and when do I use `scss:rules`?

| Section | What it does | Example from this site |
|:-----------------|:--------------------------------|:---------------------|
| `scss:defaults` | Sets Bootstrap variables before the theme is built, so changes flow through the whole site | `$primary`, `$link-color`, `$font-family-sans-serif` |
| `scss:rules` | Adds or overrides specific styles after the theme is built | `.highlight`, navbar hover color, heading underlines |

## What does it look like when it works?

This box uses a custom class from `styles.scss`. I applied it with a fenced div:

```{.markdown}
::: highlight
**Tip:** use classes for anything you reuse.
:::
```

::: highlight
**Tip:** use classes for anything you reuse. Changing the color once in `styles.scss` updates every box on the site.
:::

The heading above each section also gets the gold underline from one rule: `h1.title, h2 { border-bottom: 3px solid $farm-gold; }`.

## How do I style just one page or one element?

- **One element:** add a class or inline attributes, like `[text]{style="color:#C48A3A;"}` or `::: {.highlight}`.
- **One page:** put `css:` (or a `<style>` block) in that page's own YAML instead of the site's `_quarto.yml`.
- **Light and dark:** give the theme two files, such as `theme: {light: [cosmo, styles.scss], dark: [darkly, styles-dark.scss]}`.

## What did I learn?

Set colors and fonts once in `scss:defaults`, keep one-off tweaks in `scss:rules`, and use named classes so the content stays clean. After each change, re-render to see it.
